hook: A short file built around a cursed MiniDV tape with only a few minutes of footage on it. The description is brief; the part that stays with you is the recorded testimony of an exposed subject reading aloud that follows it. Deaths by choking are described flatly throughout, including in a recording of a children's stage show.
whyItMatters: It is a compact example of a media-borne hazard where the object is harmless and the damage lies in everything the viewer watches, hears or reads afterwards. Because the effect reaches into fiction itself, a page this short manages to suggest an entire lifetime of consequences. The Foundation's response is notably small: a steel safe, a lethal security system, and a note that exposed D-class may be kept alive for long-term psychological study.
thingsToNotice: The timestamped tape summary looks routine until a costumed performer in a silent Sesame Street Live recording begins to choke and struggles to pull his costume off; over the following nineteen seconds three more characters die the same way. Afterwards, every character the viewer meets in any medium, real or fictional, dies of asphyxiation in their perception, permanently. The French testimony demonstrates it: reading A Clash of Kings aloud, the subject watches Aggo and then Dany die, then reads a Carambar wrapper joke in which the chicken chokes halfway across the road, and laughs. His offhand remark that he will need a book with lots of characters is the most unsettling line on the page.
